Arjun —

Great, thanks for the clear list. Attaching our VPC config template and the current on-prem manifest (PDF) for your facilities team. Monica (solutions engineer) and Ben (ops lead) are looped for technical details and scheduling.

Quick answers up front:
- Recommendation: VPC peering for sub-1ms intra-region traffic (US central) and simpler routing; PrivateLink if you require enforced ZTNA + per-service endpoints. We’ll provide a mapping doc for both.
- NAT: Redwood expects stable egress IPs from your NAT/gateway for outbound webhook callbacks; we can also support source-IP allowlisting if you prefer.
- MTU: Default 1500; if you have jumbo frames we can adjust but need confirmation of end-to-end MTU.
- BGP: Not required unless you want dynamic failover for appliance VPN; we support BGP ASN negotiation for partner-managed routers.

Monica — can you draft the technical checklist (CIDR allocation, route table entries, SGs, firewall ports, TLS termination point, expected SYN throughput, and any appliance power/networking constraints)? Also note the appliance needs 2U rack space, 2x 10G SFP+ uplinks by default (details in manifest).

Arjun — I’ll follow up with a proposed 30-minute netops call later this week to walk the checklist.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Arjun / netops team —

Posting the technical checklist here so your engineers can copy/paste into a ticket:

1) CIDR & routing
   - Preferred setup: allocate a /22 from your VPC for Redwood peering (example: 10.40.0.0/22). This keeps host ranges small and leaves room for expansion.
   - If you need overlapping ranges, we’ll route via PrivateLink or SNAT — we can discuss mapping.

2) Routes & peering
   - Create a VPC peering connection to aws-account: 123456789012 (Redwood PE) in us-central-1.
   - Add a route for Redwood CIDR -> peering connection in your route table.

3) Firewall & security groups
   - Required outbound: 443/TCP to 52.12.34.0/24 (Redwood public egress pool) for control-plane callbacks.
   - Required inbound (if using peering and private endpoints): 10250-10260/TCP (control tunnel), 443/TCP (TLS), plus management port 22022/TCP if you want direct SSH to appliance mgmt.

4) NAT & egress
   - If you NAT outbound from your datacenter, provide the stable egress IPs so we can create allowlist entries.
   - For appliance-hosted outbound traffic, specify whether you will SNAT to a public IP or route through your corporate proxy.

5) VPN & BGP
   - VPN mode: IPsec site-to-site supported. If you prefer dynamic routing, we recommend setting up BGP sessions (Redwood ASN 64512 by default) and advertise the appliance subnets.
   - MTU: default 1500. If using GRE or IPsec encapsulation, set effective MTU ~1420; confirm if you use jumbo frames.

6) Appliance rack/power
   - Manifest summary: 2U unit, 2x hot-swap PSUs, typical idle draw 350W, max 700W. Network: 2x 10Gb SFP+ (primary/management).
   - KVM/IPMI access required for staging (we can do initial validation over a temporary VPN).

7) Performance & QoS
   - Expected SYN rate at 100k TPS is not required for initial rollout; provide expected steady-state throughput and burst patterns.

Next steps (proposed):
- We schedule a 30min netops call to validate CIDR and egress IPs (proposed 2026-09-01 10:00 PDT).
- You share completed VPC template YAML + facility rack photo if available.
- Redwood issues a shipping manifest once manifest sign-off is complete.

We’ve included an example vpc template in the YAML attachment — please populate your CIDR and NAT IPs and send back.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
